proposed_openingText: [Enter Duke, Egeon, Jailer, Officers and other Attendants.] EGEON. Go ahead, Solinus, sentence me to die, and let the verdict of death end my sorrows along with my life. DUKE. Merchant of Syracuse, stop pleading. I won't bend our laws. The hostility and conflict that recently sprang from your Duke's vicious crackdown on merchants — our honest countrymen, who lacked the gold to ransom themselves and so sealed his harsh decrees with their blood — has shut out all pity from our stern looks. Ever since the deadly, civil-style feud between your seditious countrymen and us began, it has been formally decreed, by both the Syracusans and ourselves, that no trade is permitted between our enemy towns. Furthermore: if any native of Ephesus is seen at Syracusan markets and fairs, or if any native Syracusan comes to the bay of Ephesus, he dies. His goods are seized by the Duke, unless a thousand marks are paid to lift the penalty and ransom him. Your possessions, valued at the highest rate, can't amount to a hundred marks. Therefore, by law you are condemned to die.
